SLOOS lens update:
- Bank supply of credit: Banks reported broad-based and significant tightening of lending standards and terms in Q2 2020 for C&I loans to firms of all sizes and for CRE loans; demand for these loans weakened. This indicates bank-intermediated credit is restrictive despite improved market functioning.
- Consumer credit: Standards tightened notably for credit cards, auto, and other consumer loans, with weaker demand—consistent with households’ cautious spending and banks’ reduced risk tolerance.
- Residential mortgages: Demand strengthened (refi and purchase, especially GSE/government), but banks still tightened standards across most mortgage categories, tempering the housing tailwind.
- Outlook from banks: Respondents expected further tightening over the remainder of 2020 due to deterioration in the economic outlook and collateral values.

Implication for the Fed statement: While policy is highly accommodative and market functioning has improved, SLOOS shows ongoing tightening in bank lending that constrains the flow of credit to businesses and consumers. That makes the overall tone more negative than an FSR-only read.
